source: 1968 Chevrolet Chassis Service Manual, Steering, p.9-29

procedures.title: Steering column: realign (Corvette)
steps: Take off the upper and lower outer covers.
Take off the upper and lower extension covers.
Loosen, without removing, attaching screws F, H and J.
Loosen the 4 nuts F, 3 screws H, 2 screws K and the rag joint flange bolt J.

Keeping a gap of .30 ± .05 between the mast jacket and the inner half-round surface of the instrument panel, hold the column lower plate firmly against the front of the dash and pull support D rearward to take up the height difference between the panel and bracket B.
With the column located, torque screw assemblies H to 20 ft. lbs., then nuts F to 20 ft. lbs.
Holding the rag joint spacing at 1/4" to 3/8" (see figure 16 in the manual), torque the upper flange pinch bolt to 30 ft. lbs.
Fasten the column lower plate to the front of the dash with screws K torqued to 150 in. lbs.
Refit the upper and lower extension covers.
Refit the upper and lower outer covers.

specs.what: mast jacket to instrument panel gap

notes: The manual's text cites figure 58 for this procedure; letter callouts refer to the manual's figure.

procedures.title: Tie rods: remove and install
steps: Replace tie rod ends when they show excessive up-and-down movement or any lost motion or end play at the ball stud.
Removal: pull the cotter pins from the ball studs and remove the castellated nuts.
Free the outer ball stud by striking the steering arm at the tie rod end with a hammer while backing it with a heavy hammer or similar; pull the tie rod down out of the arm if needed.
Free the inner ball stud from the relay rod the same way.
To separate the ends from the sleeve, loosen the clamp bolts and unscrew the ends.
Installation: if the ends were removed, coat the threads with EP chassis lube and screw the ends in, each the same distance into the sleeve.
Make sure the ball stud and nut threads are completely clean and smooth, and fit neoprene seals on the ball studs.
Fit the ball studs into the steering arms and relay rod.
Fit the ball stud nuts and cotter pins, then lubricate the tie rod ends.
Set toe-in per Section 3.
notes: Each tie rod is a sleeve with two threaded ends (right- and left-hand threads) locked by clamps; the ends self-adjust for wear and need only periodic lubrication and checks that the ball studs are tight.
Dirty or rough threads can let the ball stud spin in the end while tightening the nut.
Before locking the clamp bolts, align the tie rod ends with their ball studs with each ball joint centered in its travel, or the linkage will bind.
